title: fix: correct update status and apply saved model keys
body:
## What Problem This Solves

The update UI marks unavailable version evidence as a failed check, the CLI can leave its spinner running after a failed final history read, and removing an API key immediately after saving it can wrongly report that the key changed.

## User Impact

The version badge shows **Not verified** when identity evidence is unavailable and **Failed** only for an observed mismatch. The recorded update outcome stays unchanged. CLI progress releases its resources while preserving the original ledger-read error. Saving a model API key waits for the Gateway to apply changed provider settings before reporting normal success; an unconfirmed application returns a warning while preserving the saved key.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the report's existing identity classifier for the badge and dispose the CLI observer and spinner in `finally`. Remove a copied translation catalog that had drifted from the real English strings, a redundant test, unnecessary type assertions and guards, and explanatory comment repetition. Keep the receipt, recovery, localization, and connection-ownership coverage. API-key saving now uses the existing configuration application receipt and originating request continuation, as credential removal already does. Authentication refresh consumes the applied configuration. Concurrent binding/credential guards and disabled-reload policy remain unchanged.

Update execution, schemas, stored outcomes, and installed-updater behavior are unchanged. Historical `versionMatch: false` records use the classification already established by #147553.

Related: #147993, #147553, #148769, #148790.

## Evidence

- The real-spinner regression fails before the fix with one leaked timer and passes afterward, retaining error propagation and signal-listener cleanup.
- Two missing-identity badge cases fail before and pass afterward; actual version/build mismatches remain failures.
- All 202 selected CLI, report, UI, recovery, campaign, interlock, and connection-race cases pass, including a repeat after refreshing the pinned dependencies.
- Independent P2 review and full changed-file validation pass, including core/UI/test types, lint, schema, import-cycle, and ownership guards.
- CI exposed a contradictory coalesced-restart fixture: it said expected 2.0.0/running 1.0.0 but stored 1.0.0 for both. The fixture now records the installed 2.0.0 and observed 1.0.0; both event orderings still require a failed badge. All nine bundled coalesced/update-run browser cases pass, along with the focused changed checks and independent P2 review.
- The synthetic Settings/Updates proof uses the actual UI with a mocked Gateway and makes zero `update.run` requests. The inspected before/after screenshots below are also attached in the originating chat.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Missing identity shown as Failed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/90dfbbf2-b7de-4a33-9317-f11b42c95336) | ![Missing identity shown as Not verified](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8c03a1f1-fff4-40f8-b2a1-5d657ee056ff) |

### Version badge detail

The Version badge changes from **Failed** to **Not verified**. The failed update headline and failed verification phase remain recorded facts. These four-times-enlarged crops are taken directly from the original screenshots above.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Enlarged Version badge: Failed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/59d9682e-70b1-4d7c-9c74-120057f5eb6e) | ![Enlarged Version badge: Not verified](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5f09d089-14e0-4f61-876c-8350851d65f7) |

### Additional qualification repairs

- A delayed-publication regression fails before the API-key repair because Save completes before application. Afterward Save remains pending, then immediate removal succeeds. All 220 selected auth, CLI, Gateway and removal tests pass, including application/refresh warnings, unchanged bindings and concurrent credential preservation. Independent P2 review and full changed checks pass. A fresh build of the old save/RPC/CLI source reproduces the same removal rejection as CI; the candidate passes the entire real-Gateway UI and CLI save/remove flow with identical durable states. The capture run uses a taller 1280×1100 viewport so result messages are visible; all existing actions, assertions, deadlines and cleanup are unchanged.
- Two capacity fixes landed on main during qualification (#148843 and #148861). Their combined tree overfilled services to 702 roots. Return the 44 heartbeat roots to infrastructure while keeping update lifecycle tests in services: services drops to 658 and infrastructure rises from 560 to 604. All 10,601 canonical roots remain assigned exactly once with the same inventory digest; the 700-root guard, 720-root hard cap, graph count and runtime routing are unchanged. Both affected compiler graphs, all 24 partition tests, scoped checks and independent P2 review pass.
- Earlier CI also hit an unchanged Gateway readiness timeout (passed in the next run) and a proxy-capture child timeout whose logs do not establish a cause. No deadline or assertion was weakened. Current-head CI must pass before landing.

### Model API-key save and removal

The real Gateway flow reproduces the false concurrent-change error before the repair and completes removal afterward. These inspected crops show the provider and result message; the same images are attached in the originating chat. The fixture uses synthetic credentials and isolated state.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![API-key removal incorrectly rejected](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4c0d30db-b1a6-49ca-ba42-b5dbede7c89a) | ![API key successfully removed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3b332107-7a01-4b4b-af90-7690e8be5d40) |

### Automation fixture alignment

CI on `4300ae7e0d97` passed the model API-key scenario and 133 jobs. Its sole test failure was the automation-management fixture: it configured both Telegram senders as owners but still expected cross-job denial after #148790 deliberately granted configured owners management authority.

Adopted @vincentkoc’s fixture repair from #148769 (`508ad6e56fa7`), preserving his credit. It verifies configured-owner list/get, a true non-owner’s absent automation capability with unchanged job/run state and zero management audit, and all five Control UI administrator actions. Local execution also caught the fixture’s empty-tool precheck; allowing the existing `session_status` tool lets the non-owner reach the mock provider while `automations` remains unavailable.

The final real-Gateway scenario passes with synthetic Crabline Telegram transport, a deterministic provider, and seven expected management audit events. All original deadlines remain unchanged. Scoped types/lint/guards and independent P2 review pass. This updates test expectations for existing policy; production permission logic is unchanged. The final rebased API-key flow also passes with the unmodified 1280×900 E2E test.
